For the Poincare consumer the supplier matches: both Statements assume smooth autonomous field on an open Euclidean set; F2 and proof1.1–2.1 use common local times and state differentiation, then finite composition along the periodic segment. However the Hopf consumer Statement assumes only C5 f; its F6 calls the supplier smooth flow, and steps2.1/4.1 use flow/variational differentiation/uniqueness. The provider Statement requires smooth (=C-infinity, as explicitly defined in def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms). C5 does not supply this hypothesis. Poincare F8 specializes this to metric spaces, and proof3.1/4.1 applies it to the continuous flow on a compact time/closed-section product containing (0,a). Supplier gives expprime(z)=exp(z) for every complex z. Restriction along the affine real path gives d/dt exp(alpha t)=alpha exp(alpha t), consistent with componentwise chain rules already used there. Entire domain has no pole/branch or field restriction; this is actual derivative use, not a citation to a matrix exponential theorem.

Delay-history consumer Statement uses real C([-tau,0],R^d), d>=1,tau>0, and F4/proof3.1 applies exactly that definition. Proof1.1 obtains completeness in d_infinity from its separate curve-space supplier;2.1 verifies the real sup norm and shows its induced metric equals d_infinity. CQ generating lemma proof1.1 bounds |omega_j|<=1 and uses geometric comparison for all r<1 to establish radius>=1; F3 then applies the provider only for |z|<1 to make W holomorphic. The supplier allows arbitrary complex coefficients and no Choice axiom; the consumer real coefficients are valid special cases. No boundary |z|=1 differentiation is claimed.

All three providers have this actual published A home and each is concretely used. Generating lemma F7/2.1 uses the unit-disc definition |z|<1 (not Blaschke-factor properties). F8/1.3 uses the branch-power definition exp(alpha Log(1-z)); it first excludes 1-z on the nonpositive real axis, so the holomorphic slit-plane domain condition is satisfied. Principal-positive-real-power theorem requires positive real base and real exponent: generating lemma2.1 and weights lemma F11/proof2.1 use real x in(-1,1), so base1-x>0 and alpha real. Quadratic coefficient lemma F2/proof2.1 uses that same real-interval identity via weights. Neither negative-axis pointwise principal values nor a complex power law across branches is imported.

Both suppliers are on the actual published A winding/Cauchy page. Star-shaped-domain proposition requires nonempty open star-shaped subset of C; generating lemma F7/2.1 takes unit disc, containing0, open and convex hence star-shaped about0, to obtain complex-domain connectedness. Principal-log corollary gives holomorphic Log specifically on S=C minus nonpositive real axis. Proof1.3 shows1-z belongs to S for |z|<1 by contradiction with |z|>=1, then invokes holomorphy there. It makes no claim of holomorphic Log on all nonzero C or across the cut; these are genuine domain prerequisites.

All three derivative providers are on the actual published A complex-differentiability page. Generating lemma F9/proof1.3 constructs P(z)=exp(alpha Log(1-z)). Affine1-z is holomorphic by algebra theorem constant/identity/scalar rules, inner image lies in open slit plane by the explicit exclusion argument, Log is holomorphic there, scalar alpha multiplication is holomorphic, and exponential is entire. Chain-rule provider open-domain and evaluation-point requirements are therefore met successively; algebra/exponential supply precisely the stated operations, with complex field throughout and no additional axiom hypothesis.

Actual published A identity/open-mapping page contains thm-identity-theorem-holomorphic-functions. Provider requires two holomorphic functions on one connected complex domain with agreement set accumulating inside it. Generating lemma2.1 takes D unit disc; prior1.1 and1.3 establish W,P holomorphic, F7 supplies that D is a domain, and1.2 plus principal-real bridge give W=P on real(-1,1). This interval accumulates at0 in D. Thus the exact provider hypotheses hold; equality is extended only through D, not to the unit-circle boundary.
